changes: quorum_submit now persists the complete three-round-by-two-host verdict batch as one exact six-line metadata commit, shares a cooperative process-event writer lock, and rolls back only its owned bytes on failure.
usage: Run the worktree-local quorum_submit after all current reviewer lanes pass; a successful response reports emittedCount=6 and metadataCommitSha, and leaves git clean.
expectedOutcome: One successful quorum submission creates exactly one commit containing six host_verdict rows and no unrelated file changes.
actualTranscript: git show --numstat e764c1cd18 returned 6 additions, 0 deletions, only .lattice/story/actives/B-6ed2/process-events.jsonl; the post-command worktree was clean.
outcomeDiff: No difference: the observed commit exactly matched the expected six-row single-file transaction.
pitfalls: Closeout evidence commits invalidated reviewer receipts once, requiring metadata-only incremental re-attestation. A live-smoke wrapper imposed a 60-second outer timeout on DONE-required, so the formal command was rerun directly with its legal 1200-second suite budget. After merging main, validate lineage also falsely proposed a redundant full rerun; it was stopped after 37 seconds and the existing PASS remained valid under unchanged storyFilesHash.
